articles.summary: Doctors in New Delhi describe an elderly patient whose anxiety episodes drove him to seek physical restraint for relief. A literature search turned up no comparable case in older adults.

articles.title: Antagonistic and impulsive traits are linked to cyberbullying, trolling, and catfishing on Instagram
articles.summary: Maladaptive personality traits may help explain who engages in harmful behavior online. Among Instagram-using students in Iran, antagonism and impulsivity were tied to cyberbullying and trolling, while negative emotionality was tied to Instagram addiction.

articles.title: Prolonged mask exposure changes how we process facial emotions
articles.summary: A longitudinal study reveals that people adapt to reading emotions on mask-covered faces over time. The findings show improvements in identifying occluded expressions of fear and happiness, highlighting the adaptability of human social cognition.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive
articles.summary: Exercising too much without adequate recovery may disrupt brain chemistry in surprising ways. Scientists found that mice subjected to prolonged, intense training had elevated dopamine levels in a brain region linked to memory and emotions, even 48 hours after exercising. The discovery could help explain why overtrained athletes sometimes struggle with insomnia, anxiety, and persistent fatigue, although these symptoms were not directly measured.

articles.title: The earlier kids join social media, the lower their test scores tend to be, study finds
articles.summary: When should kids get social media? A study tracking more than 5,000 Italian students’ test scores from 2nd to 10th grade found that those who joined earlier tended to fall further behind in Italian and math.

articles.summary: New eye-tracking research suggests people start registering a face emoji's expression in peripheral vision before looking directly at it, pausing slightly longer on the preceding word while finishing the overall sentence faster.

articles.summary: A newly validated gender-role measure indicates that beliefs about whether men should be breadwinners are closely tied to women's feminist identity and willingness to confront everyday sexism, outperforming an older survey.

articles.title: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard
articles.summary: A study of more than 10,000 college students found that exercising regularly may be more important for mental health than pushing yourself through intense or lengthy workouts. Students who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety a year later, suggesting that consistency could be a key ingredient in protecting mental well-being.

articles.title: This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's
articles.summary: Reading for pleasure may have surprisingly powerful benefits for the brain, with studies linking it to better memory, reduced stress, improved mental health, and a lower risk of dementia. Researchers highlight findings that just five minutes of fiction can reduce stress by up to 20%, while reading has also been associated with a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

articles.title: An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.25070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven framework, CodeReAct agent, designed to enhance industrial equipment maintenance through natural language (NL) interactions. The framework employs an advanced AI agentic approach to interpret human instructions, providing knowledge extraction, asset status summarization, and work order recommendations. It identifies patterns and trends and predicts work orders by standardizing industrial data into business objects (BOs) and utilizing analytical function API calls. The AI agent operates through a Thought-Action-Obs

articles.title: SailSearch: Agent-Assisted Discovery in Combinatorial Optimization
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.25087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present SailSearch, a human-guided workflow for algorithmic research with two language-model agents, and report results on Market Split and maximum independent set (MIS).
